bounded_slice.tested_scope: Exact pinned source-path reproduction for lbx154/Argus commit 2894b434affaff3a28c1fbbcd5c39f2e7a832236, limited to the CLI --ask call site in argus_skill/apps/cli/_core.py, manager.config_intent._front_door_classify, Manager._task_usage_scope in argus_skill/manager/_core.py, and Manager.classify_front_door in argus_skill/manager/_front_door_ops.py. The question is only whether a non-null mission_id is bound before the first Manager backend execution on this exact CLI --ask path.
observations: The exact CLI --ask path calls _front_door_classify(bundle, question, chat_state) without a root_task_id argument.
_front_door_classify defaults root_task_id to None and only forwards root_task_id into mgr.classify_front_door when root_task_id is non-null and the method accepts that parameter.
Therefore the exact CLI --ask call invokes Manager.classify_front_door without root_task_id.
Manager.classify_front_door performs the classifier backend call inside `with self._task_usage_scope(root_task_id)`.
Manager._task_usage_scope returns nullcontext() when root_task_id is falsey, so the supplied usage_context factory is not entered for this call.

The runner constructor previously established project/global usage context with mission_id=None; this exact first CLI --ask Manager backend execution does not rebind it to a non-null mission_id before the backend call.
bounded_slice.acceptance_effect: For the exact pinned CLI --ask path, the first Manager classification backend execution is not mission-scoped: the call chain omits root_task_id, causing Manager._task_usage_scope(None) to use nullcontext while the constructor-level usage context remains mission_id=None. This is an exact-scope counterexample to any claim that every first Manager backend execution is non-null mission-bound. It does not establish behavior for other callers that do supply root_task_id.
exclusions: No claim is made about Web/API, life-chat, or other callers of _front_door_classify.
